data.title: We Think Pioneer Power Solutions (NASDAQ:PPSI) Needs To Drive Business Growth Carefully
data.description:
We can readily understand why investors are attracted to unprofitable companies. For example, although Amazon.com made losses for many years after listing, if you had bought and held the shares since 1999, you would have made a fortune. But while history lauds those rare successes, those that fail are often forgotten; who remembers Pets.com?

So should Pioneer Power Solutions (NASDAQ:PPSI) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? For the purpose of this article, we'll define cash burn as the amount of cash the company is spending each year to fund its growth (also called its negative free cash flow). We'll start by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves in order to calculate its cash runway.

When Might Pioneer Power Solutions Run Out Of Money?

A cash runway is defined as the length of time it would take a company to run out of money if it kept spending at its current rate of cash burn. As at September 2026, Pioneer Power Solutions had cash of US$9.4m and no debt. Importantly, its cash burn was US$8.1m over the trailing twelve months. So it had a cash runway of approximately 14 months from September 2026. That's not too bad, but it's fair to say the end of the cash runway is in sight, unless cash burn reduces drastically. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

Check out our latest analysis for Pioneer Power Solutions

How Well Is Pioneer Power Solutions Growing?

We reckon the fact that Pioneer Power Solutions managed to shrink its cash burn by 26% over the last year is rather encouraging. Unfortunately, however, operating revenue declined by 37% during the period. In light of the data above, we're fairly sanguine about the business growth trajectory. Clearly, however, the crucial factor is whether the company will grow its business going forward. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

Can Pioneer Power Solutions Raise More Cash Easily?

Pioneer Power Solutions seems to be in a fairly good position, in terms of cash burn, but we still think it's worthwhile considering how easily it could raise more money if it wanted to. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. Many companies end up issuing new shares to fund future growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

Pioneer Power Solutions has a market capitalisation of US$23m and burnt through US$8.1m last year, which is 35% of the company's market value. That's not insignificant, and if the company had to sell enough shares to fund another year's growth at the current share price, you'd likely witness fairly costly dilution.

Is Pioneer Power Solutions' Cash Burn A Worry?

Even though its falling revenue makes us a little nervous, we are compelled to mention that we thought Pioneer Power Solutions' cash burn reduction was relatively promising. data.title: Will Bonterra Resources (CVE:BTR) Spend Its Cash Wisely?
data.description:
We can readily understand why investors are attracted to unprofitable companies. For example, although Amazon.com made losses for many years after listing, if you had bought and held the shares since 1999, you would have made a fortune. Having said that, unprofitable companies are risky because they could potentially burn through all their cash and become distressed.

So should Bonterra Resources (CVE:BTR) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? In this report, we will consider the company's annual negative free cash flow, henceforth referring to it as the 'cash burn'. First, we'll determine its cash runway by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves.

When Might Bonterra Resources Run Out Of Money?

A company's cash runway is the amount of time it would take to burn through its cash reserves at its current cash burn rate. As at September 2026, Bonterra Resources had cash of CA$15m and no debt. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through CA$13m. So it had a cash runway of approximately 14 months from September 2026. While that cash runway isn't too concerning, sensible holders would be peering into the distance, and considering what happens if the company runs out of cash. How Is Bonterra Resources' Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Because Bonterra Resources isn't currently generating revenue, we consider it an early-stage business. So while we can't look to sales to understand growth, we can look at how the cash burn is changing to understand how expenditure is trending over time. Over the last year its cash burn actually increased by a very significant 89%. While this spending increase is no doubt intended to drive growth, if the trend continues the company's cash runway will shrink very quickly. Bonterra Resources makes us a little nervous due to its lack of substantial operating revenue. We prefer most of the stocks on this list of stocks that analysts expect to grow.

Can Bonterra Resources Raise More Cash Easily?

While Bonterra Resources does have a solid cash runway, its cash burn trajectory may have some shareholders thinking ahead to when the company may need to raise more cash. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. Many companies end up issuing new shares to fund future growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

Bonterra Resources has a market capitalisation of CA$46m and burnt through CA$13m last year, which is 28% of the company's market value. That's fairly notable cash burn, so if the company had to sell shares to cover the cost of another year's operations, shareholders would suffer some costly dilution.

Is Bonterra Resources' Cash Burn A Worry?

QUALCOMM now has multi year capital locked in at known coupons, which can support heavier R&D and capacity commitments tied to its US$5b fiscal 2027 and US$15b fiscal 2029 AI data center revenue targets.

For you as a shareholder, that new debt stack raises the execution bar on projects such as the AWS custom silicon and optical connectivity agreement, which the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St views as a core driver of future non handset QCT revenue. If those design wins ramp more slowly than planned, higher interest costs and elevated operating expenses could weigh more heavily on earnings and keep valuation sensitive to any setback in AI centric programs.

QUALCOMM's narrative projects US$62.7b revenue and US$12.3b earnings by 2029, which implies forecast revenue growth of 13.3% per year and an earnings decline of US$1.3b from current earnings of US$13.6b.

Exploring Other Perspectives

The most cautious analysts were projecting about US$58.1b of sales and US$11.8b of earnings by 2029, yet still saw a sharply lower fair value. data.title: Nasdaq (NDAQ) Just Gave Investors Something To Think About

data.title: Is Honeywell International (HON) Cheaper After A 46% Slide?
data.description:
Honeywell International has seen its share price fall sharply year to date, and that slide puts a fresh spotlight on whether the cash the business can generate really lines up with where the stock now trades. With a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) estimate available, investors are increasingly focused on how Honeywell's current price stacks up against the long term cash flows its operations may support.

  • The stock is down 45.7% year to date, which puts the recent selloff front and center for anyone asking if the move reflects a reset in expectations for Honeywell's future cash generation.
  • Recent updates on automation, physical AI and smart building platforms, along with a reported backlog of nearly US$19b, may support views on the durability and timing of Honeywell's cash inflows from these growth areas.
  • What if you looked at Honeywell International through its earnings instead? See why Honeywell International's 7.5x P/E tells a different valuation story.

The issue now is whether Honeywell's current share price is justified by the cash flows implied by its intrinsic value estimate under the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach.

If you want a yardstick for Honeywell International's AI driven automation and cash flow story, compare it with the 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Does Honeywell International Look Pricey on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here projects what Honeywell International might generate for shareholders based on its future free cash generation. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits around $935.1m, while analyst and model estimates point to Free Cash Flow to Equity moving into the low $3b range over the next decade, then easing into slower growth. That pattern reflects a mature industrial and automation group where cash generation is expected to be sizeable but not racing higher every year.

The DCF outcome indicates Honeywell's implied intrinsic value is meaningfully below the current share price of $212.64, so the market is attaching a richer tag to the stock than the cash flow stream here would support on its own. Recent emphasis on pure play automation, physical AI and data center infrastructure, backed by a backlog near $19b, helps explain why investors may be willing to pay up despite a more measured long term cash flow glide path in the model.
